16	package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest;

18	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;
19	
20	/**
21	 * Builds an owner's customer code, formatted {@code '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>'} where
22	 * {@code CITY3} is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, {@code LAST3}
23	 * the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and {@code NNNN} a per-city
24	 * 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number of owners already
25	 * in that city, e.g. {@code 'LON-SMI-0007'}.
26	 */
27	@Component
28	public class CustomerCodeGenerator {
29	
30	    /**
31	     * Generate a customer code for a new owner.
32	     *
33	     * @param city           the owner's city; its first three letters (upper-cased) form the prefix
34	     * @param lastName       the owner's last name; its first three letters (upper-cased) form the middle segment
35	     * @param cityOwnerCount the number of owners already in that city; the sequence is one more than this value
36	     * @return the formatted customer code
37	     */
38	    public String generate(String city, String lastName, long cityOwnerCount) {
39	        return String.format("%s-%s-%04d", prefix(city), prefix(lastName), cityOwnerCount + 1);
40	    }
41	
42	    private String prefix(String value) {
43	        return value.substring(0, Math.min(3, value.length())).toUpperCase();
44	    }
45	}

20	import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner;
21	import org.springframework.stereotype.Component;

23	/**
24	 * Counts an owner's namesakes, i.e. existing owners that share the same first and last
25	 * name compared case-insensitively.
26	 */
27	@Component
28	public class NamesakeCounter {
29	
30	    /**
31	     * Count how many of the given existing owners share the candidate's first and last
32	     * name, comparing both case-insensitively.
33	     *
34	     * @param candidate      the owner about to be created
35	     * @param existingOwners owners already stored (typically pre-filtered by last name)
36	     * @return the number of existing owners sharing the candidate's first and last name
37	     */
38	    public int count(Owner candidate, Collection<Owner> existingOwners) {
39	        return (int) existingOwners.stream()
40	            .filter(existing -> existing.getFirstName().equalsIgnoreCase(candidate.getFirstName())
41	                && existing.getLastName().equalsIgnoreCase(candidate.getLastName()))
42	            .count();
43	    }
44	}

19	/**

21	 * of owner registrations. Carries the offending date so it can be logged.
22	 */
23	public class DailyOwnerLimitException extends RuntimeException {
24	
25	    /** Maximum number of owners that may be registered on a single day. */
26	    public static final long MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY = 100;
27	
28	    /** Name of the offending field, used to build the error response. */
29	    public static final String FIELD = "registrationDate";
30	
31	    public DailyOwnerLimitException(java.time.LocalDate registrationDate) {
32	        super("Day already reached the maximum of " + MAX_OWNERS_PER_DAY + " owner registrations: "
33	            + registrationDate);
34	    }
35	}

`AcceptanceTest` is the only test class, and it passes. The change is complete.

## Summary

The spec required the **effective** registration date (supplied or defaulted) to fall on a business day, rolling weekends forward to the next Monday, with all derived values using the adjusted date.

**Changes:**

1. **New `BusinessDayResolver`** (`util/BusinessDayResolver.java`) — a small single-responsibility utility, mirroring the existing `LocalityResolver` style. Its `toBusinessDay(LocalDate)` returns weekdays unchanged and rolls Saturday/Sunday forward to the next Monday via `TemporalAdjusters.next(MONDAY)`.

2. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — after the effective date is established (either supplied by the request or defaulted to `LocalDate.now()`), it now applies `BusinessDayResolver.toBusinessDay(...)` and stores the result back on the owner **before** the daily-limit check and save.

Because the adjusted date is written onto the owner up front, everything downstream automatically uses it:
- the **daily create-limit** counts owners per adjusted business day (the count uses the local `registrationDate` variable read after adjustment),
- the **membership number's year segment** (computed in `OwnerMapper` from `owner.getRegistrationDate()`) uses the adjusted date,
- the persisted/returned `registrationDate` is the business day.

This also correctly changes the prior behaviour where a supplied weekend date was kept as-is. The test suite is green.
